kind: CHARACTERISATION of the shipped engine on existing sealed data. Read-only. No vectors generated, no threshold moved, no production gate derived.
authorising_section_verbatim: SPACE-F4-MARGIN-01 - a static-carrier structural-margin study: sweep the existing catalogue families (RS, concatenated, TC-LDPC, burst, continuous stream) on static carriers across SNR and length, recording per capture the F4 best_log10_p, its bar, the margin, and the converged-codeword count of any accepted hypothesis; pre-register that any accept with zero converged codewords is a failure. Its purpose is to characterise how close the shipped engine runs to an F4 accept when nothing is drifting. It is separate from CARRIER_ESTIMATOR_EXPERIMENT.md, which records the same F4 fields (section 5, section 6.3) but only over one signal family.
question: Over the shipped engine's normal operating domain on static carriers: how close does the F4 block-code family run to its acceptance boundary, and does acceptance with zero converged codewords occur - and if it does, is the published structure wrong?

ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.ambiguity: Section 11.1.9 names the catalogue FAMILIES to sweep but does not say whether to analyse existing sealed datasets or generate new vectors.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.resolution: EXISTING SEALED DATASETS, READ-ONLY. bench-v2's sealed split already contains exactly the families named (burst, continuous stream, CCSDS concatenated, framed RS, TC LDPC CLTU) across five Es/N0 levels and two frame lengths, so it IS the population the section describes. No vector is generated; nothing is added to make a sample size more favourable.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.basis: The authorising turn's instruction: 'If it calls for existing sealed datasets, analyze them read-only' and 'Do not add arbitrary vectors simply to increase a favorable sample size.'

ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.ambiguity: 'static carriers' is not defined against bench-v2's structure, where every vector carries a static CFO drawn U(-0.008, +0.008) cyc/sample PLUS one channel class (awgn, phase_noise, cfo_drift, rician, amplitude, timing).
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.resolution: The PRIMARY static-carrier population is the awgn channel class of bench-v2 sealed, plus bench-v1 sealed (30 files, static CFO by construction) plus the independent null set (1,350 files, static CFO by construction). The remaining bench-v2 channel classes are analysed and reported SEPARATELY as context, and the two drifting classes (cfo_drift, phase_noise) are explicitly labelled non-static so they can never be read as part of the static answer.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.basis: bench2_gen.apply_channel (FACT from code); reported rather than merged.

ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.ambiguity: Vector counts and repetitions are unspecified in section 11.1.9.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.resolution: Not applicable: no vectors are generated. The population size is whatever the existing sealed datasets contain - 430 + 30 + 1,350 = 1,810 captures - and is reported as such, not chosen.

ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.ambiguity: CONFLICT, NOT MERELY AN AMBIGUITY. Section 11.1.9 pre-registers 'any accept with zero converged codewords is a failure'. The existing implementation documents the opposite reading: src/blockcode.py lines 175-177 state 'Every codeword contributes its information bits, converged or not, so the payload stays aligned with the transmission; converged_codewords says which blocks are proven consistent with H' - i.e. convergence is a per-block provenance marker, NOT an acceptance requirement. bench-v2's own scorer (eval/bench2.py, TP_PARTIAL branch) treats an LDPC accept with only some codewords converged as PARTIAL CREDIT, not as a false accept.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.resolution: THE FAILURE LABEL FROM SECTION 11.1.9 IS NOT APPLIED IN THIS EXPERIMENT. Zero-convergence accepts are COUNTED AND CHARACTERISED, and judged only on whether the PUBLISHED STRUCTURE IS WRONG against ground truth. This is a deliberate, recorded departure from the wording of section 11.1.9, made before any measurement was taken, and it is reported prominently in the results.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.basis: The authorising turn's instruction: 'Do not assume that zero convergence is inherently unsafe unless the existing F4 logic/specification establishes that interpretation. Report the actual evidence.' The existing logic establishes the opposite interpretation, so the section-11.1.9 label is unsupported and is not used as a bar.

ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.ambiguity: Section 11.1.9 says 'the margin' without defining its sign or formula.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.resolution: The repository's existing convention is used verbatim: eval/ladder.py line 65 computes log10p_margin = accept.log10_p - accept.log10_threshold. Therefore MARGIN = best_log10_p - bar, where a NEGATIVE margin means the hypothesis CLEARED the bar (was accepted) and a POSITIVE margin means it fell short. No new metric is invented.
ambiguities_and_declared_resolutions.basis: eval/ladder.py:65 (FACT from code); the authorising turn's instruction to use the repository's existing definition.

population.arm: SHIPPED ENGINE ONLY - analyze_iq(iq) unmodified. No ablation, no pre-correction, no oracle. The tracking-ablated arm A of SPACE-DOPPLER-MECH-01 is NOT used as a substitute for the shipped engine anywhere in this experiment.

datasets.name: bench-v2 sealed
datasets.role: the catalogue families named in section 11.1.9, across Es/N0 {3,6,9,12,15} and all six channel classes; the awgn subset is the primary static population

datasets.name: bench-v1 sealed
datasets.role: the documented regression tripwire; static CFO by construction

datasets.name: independent null set
datasets.role: non-catalogue control, static CFO by construction: any F4 accept here is a structural false accept

not_in_population: data/space_bench/doppler (the sealed 192-vector SPACE-DOPPLER experiment) - IMMUTABLE, not read or re-scored by this experiment

data/space_bench/doppler_mech (the 144-capture SPACE-DOPPLER-MECH-01 experiment) - IMMUTABLE; its published F4 margins stand as reported in results/space_doppler_mech_f4_margins.jsonl and are quoted, not recomputed
data/bench2/calibration and data/bench2/train - out of scope: the question concerns the shipped engine's behaviour on sealed evidence

margin_definition: margin = F4 best_log10_p - F4 log10_threshold (eval/ladder.py:65 convention). Negative = accepted. Reported per capture; summarised as min / median / count within declared distances of zero, with no bar applied.
recorded_fields: dataset, file, class / family / expected (from each dataset's own ground-truth sidecar)
channel class and Es/N0 where the dataset records them; static vs non-static label per AMB-2
F4 best_log10_p, F4 bar, margin, accepted flag
accepted hypothesis identity: code name, family (rs | ldpc), offset or (E, I, Q), randomizer
n_codewords, n_converged, and the zero-convergence flag
count and reasons of F4 significant_but_rejected entries
F2 accepted flag and its code, so 'which family supplied the published code' is answerable
final status, final published code and modulation
ground-truth correctness of the published structure (scoring per dataset, below)

correctness_scoring.bench-v2 sealed: eval/bench2.py::_score, imported VERBATIM - the repository's own definition of a correct claim on those captures (TP / TP_PARTIAL / FALSE_ACCEPT / FN / REFUSED_OK). No bench-v2 criterion is evaluated, no bench-v2 file is written, and no entry is added to eval/bench2_access_log.jsonl, because this is a per-file diagnostic and not a criteria run.
correctness_scoring.bench-v1 sealed: as sealed_test.py defines it: correct = DECODED with a conv K7 claim and payload BER < 0.01 against the recorded original_bits, using bench2._ber.
correctness_scoring.null set: as eval/nullset.py defines it: correct = refusal. ANY DECODED is a structural false accept.

characterisation_questions: Q1 - What is the distribution of the F4 margin over the shipped engine on this population, and which captures come closest to the bar without clearing it?
Q2 - How many F4 acceptances occur, on which captures, and with what converged-codeword counts?
Q3 - Does any F4 acceptance have ZERO converged codewords, and if so was the published structure correct against ground truth?
Q4 - Does an F4 acceptance ever supply a WRONG published code or modulation on a legitimate capture in the shipped configuration?
no_tuning_clause: No acceptance bar is moved. ALPHA, the family weights, F2_AGREEMENT_FLOOR, CFO_MAX and TRACK_MIN_SYMBOLS are untouched.
No new threshold is introduced, and no convergence requirement is added anywhere.
Hypothesis enumeration and the F1 -> F4 -> F2 resolution order are unchanged.
No production gate, and no candidate production change, may be derived from this experiment. It answers 'what does the shipped system currently do', not 'how do we make the result pass'.
No file under src/, server/, frontend/, deploy/, Dockerfile or requirements.txt is modified.
escalation_rule: Declared before measurement: an F4 acceptance that supplies a WRONG published code or modulation on a legitimate (catalogue) capture in the SHIPPED configuration, or ANY F4 acceptance on a null-set capture, is a structural false accept in normal operation and escalates the open STOP bar. A zero-convergence accept whose published structure is CORRECT is NOT an escalation (see AMB-4); it is reported as a characterisation finding.
immutability: SPACE-DOPPLER (192 vectors, manifest f9823ef5a45c97f106825ac51768b9412db5c65460d3574cd06b813627fe50ea): not read, not regenerated, not re-scored, not overwritten.

SPACE-DOPPLER-MECH-01 (144 captures, manifest a152d682a811f973f4c4c14b...): not regenerated, not re-scored; its results stand as published, and section 11 of DOPPLER_MECHANISM_RESULTS.md including section 11.1 is not rewritten.
bench-v1, bench-v2 and the null set: read-only. No dataset, seed, criteria file, manifest, threshold or log of theirs is written.
outputs: results/f4_margin_rows.jsonl - one row per capture (machine-readable evidence)

revision_history.change: initial protocol: population, arm, margin definition, recorded fields, correctness scoring, characterisation questions, the five declared ambiguity resolutions (including AMB-4, which declines to apply section 11.1.9's zero-convergence failure label and states why), the no-tuning clause and the escalation rule - all committed before the harness existed and before any measurement was taken
